column1: # The red run: this tree's assertions against the engine the base ref holds,
# written whole by tests/red, which tests/run --record-assertions calls.
#   base  <ref>  <sha>  <engine version there>
#   run   <failed>  <passed>  <skipped>        lines counted, not the summary
#   <assertion name>  <times it failed>        failed names only
#   an assertion the manifest lists that the base run never reached counts as failed, by its shortfall
# A base of - means no complete red run was made: none was possible, the
# suite stopped before reached or reached no assertion, or tests/red itself
# was stopped; its stdout said which unless it was the one stopped.
# Reproduce with: tests/red <ref>
base
run
and does not list them under the header for capabilities nothing declares, but names each routine and its capability on a line of its own
and felix stack apply without --yes says how many could not be read before saying nothing changed
and for a routine with a check prints unknown with cadence 0, and does not run the check
and names those rows on a line of their own, each with its state or no state
and says how many routines could not be read in place of Nothing due
and says how many steps could not be checked in place of Nothing outstanding
and says it again on the next session start, not once per topology
and while they are unread it does not say the receipt line that is said once per topology, nor spend it
felix maintenance renders a routine it could not read as ? and not read, not as not yet
felix setup renders a step it could not check as [?] with the reason, not as not needed yet
felix stack apply --yes says how many could not be read and returns 1, though no install failed
felix stack plan prints the row it could not read as unknown, and after its summary says how many could not be read
felix_maint_status prints unknown, not dormant, for a routine on a clock whose declared list could not be read
felix_maint_unreachable says unknown in a third column for each routine whose declared list could not be read
felix_next rank 6 says the declared list could not be read for that routine, naming its capability and felix maintenance, never that nothing declares it
felix_next says at rank 6 that whether a routine on ci is due is not known when the declared list could not be read, and says the routine it named with its capability once
felix_pulse_report prints an unknown line naming the routines whose declared list could not be read
felix_setup_status prints unknown, not dormant, for a step whose declared list could not be read, and does not run its check
felix_stack_plan prints unknown, not dormant, for a row whose declared list could not be read, naming its capability
session start does not put a provider row whose state is unknown, or which has no state, among what a session owes
with only unread provider rows session start prints no paragraph saying a session owes anything, and still names them
